steps.title: Prepare Coverslips
steps.instruction: Clean and prepare the coverslips for bead deposition.

substeps.instruction: Immerse the coverslip in 1M HCl and agitate for 30 min at room temperature.
Rinse the coverslip twice with 250 mL of distilled water.
Immerse in 100% Ethanol for storage.

steps.title: Prepare Bead Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a diluted solution of fluorescent beads, ensuring no aggregates are present.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the bead stock solution for a few seconds, then vortex for 2 to 3 minutes (alternatively, sonicate in a water bath for 2 minutes at room temperature).

For ThermoFisher 175 nm beads (P7220): Perform a 1:2500 dilution by mixing 5 μL stock + 495 μL H2O (Dilution 1), then mixing 20 μL of Dilution 1 + 480 μL H2O (Final solution), resulting in ~1.2 x 10^6 beads/ml.
Optional: To aid focusing, add 1 μL of a 1:4 dilution of ThermoFisher 1 μm TetraSpeck (T7282) beads to the final 175 nm solution.

steps.title: Deposit Beads on Coverslip
steps.instruction: Apply the bead solution to the coverslip and dry.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 10 μL of the bead solution as small mini-droplets across a cleaned, air-dried coverslip.
Allow coverslips to air-dry at room temperature in a dust-free environment (e.g., laminar flow hood) for at least one hour. Do not use heat to speed up evaporation.

steps.title: Mount Coverslip to Slide
steps.instruction: Mount the dried coverslip onto a microscope slide using a compatible medium.

substeps.instruction: Clean microscope slides with 100% Ethanol and lens tissue; air dry.

Place a drop of mounting medium (e.g., 12 μL for a 22 x 22 mm coverslip) in the center of the slide. Use a medium matching the objective (e.g., high RI for oil, glycerol for glycerol, agarose for water). Warm viscous media to 37 °C if necessary.
Place the coverslip bead-side down onto the medium, lowering from one side to push bubbles to the edge.
Gently remove excess medium and bubbles with lens tissue.
Cure the medium in the dark at room temperature (e.g., Prolong Gold requires at least 24h; 48h is recommended for a stable RI of 1.46).

steps.title: Seal and Stabilize Sample
steps.instruction: Seal the sample and allow it to reach thermal equilibrium.

substeps.instruction: Seal the coverslip edge with Picodent or other two-component silicone; avoid nail varnish.
Allow the sample and room temperature to stabilize. Recommended room temperature is 23 °C.
Measure and record the temperature at the sample stage and room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare Microscope and Objective
steps.instruction: Clean the optics and warm up the system.

substeps.instruction: Clean the objective lens with 70% Ethanol wetted lens tissue, then wipe with a dry piece of lens tissue.
Reinsert the objective in the turret and set the correction collar to the correct value.
Warm up the entire system (including lasers) for 1 hour prior to imaging.

steps.title: Configure Microscope Settings
steps.instruction: Set the optical parameters for PSF acquisition based on the system type.

substeps.instruction: Select a high NA objective (e.g., 63x/1.4 for Confocal, 100x/1.4 for Spinning Disk/Widefield).
For LSMs: Set the pinhole to be wide open and use a zoom of at least 2x to center the FoV.
For Spinning Disk/Widefield: Limit the camera capture area to the center of the FoV (10 x 10 μm to 30 x 30 μm).
Set voxel size: For LSMs with NA > 1.3, use 40x40x100 nm (or up to 80x80x200 nm for routine QC). For Widefield, z-voxels can extend to 200 nm.

steps.title: Acquire Bead Images
steps.instruction: Locate and capture z-stacks of isolated beads.

substeps.instruction: Place sample on stage with sufficient immersion medium.
Focus on beads using epifluorescence (GFP/FITC filter); locate an area with sparse beads (spacing ≥ 4 μm).
Ensure at least one bead is in the center of the FoV (e.g., 30 x 30 μm area).
Optimize excitation power (488 nm laser or FITC filter) and detector gain/exposure to avoid saturation and clipping at zero.
For LSMs: Use single direction mode with averaging or increased pixel dwell time. Set PMT offset so no pixels read zero at the focal plane (unless using GaAsP/HyD detectors).
Set z-stack parameters: For LSM/Spinning Disk, capture 5 μm with 100 nm step size (51 slices). For Widefield, capture 10 μm with 200 nm step size (51 steps).
Capture images of at least 6 beads (ideally 20), ensuring beads are separated by at least 10 FWHM in all dimensions.
Verify no focal drift occurred by checking the central focal plane after acquisition.

steps.title: Analyze PSFs with MetroloJ-QC
steps.instruction: Process the acquired images using the MetroloJ-QC plugin in Fiji.

substeps.instruction: Open Fiji, start MetroloJ-QC plugin, and install iText via the 'i' icon for PDF reports.
Run either the single image PSF calibration or the batch multi-image option (selecting the raw image directory).
Enter/verify metadata: voxel size, excitation/emission wavelengths, objective NA, image bit depth, and pinhole size.
Set analysis parameters: bead size, ROI around the bead, and prominence value (determined empirically from image background).
Optionally enable the automatic discard of saturated beads.
Run the analysis to calculate FWHM along x, y, and z axes using 1D Gaussian fitting.

steps.title: Evaluate Results
steps.instruction: Interpret the calculated metrics to assess microscope quality.

substeps.instruction: Review the summary.xls and PDF reports for mean FWHM, standard deviations, SBR, and goodness of fit (r²).
Keep FWHM values only if the Gaussian r² is > 0.95; otherwise, visually inspect for aberrations.
Check the measured-to-theoretical FWHM ratio against tolerance values.
Calculate the Lateral Asymmetry Ratio (LAR) as the ratio of minimal to maximal xy FWHM.
Plot data as box and whisker plots to track performance over time.
